items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names reveal intent (durabilityTracker, satisfiedLocked, wakeLocked, fireBatchDurable, batchDurableState). Public types and methods have doc comments, and the non-obvious points are commented, e.g. why the WAL ordering means lower seqnums are durable and why errors beat ctx cancellation. Formatting passes crlfmt/lint.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The new durability.go is 502 lines, over the 500-line cap. Detecting a configured handler relies on a reflect pointer comparison ('reflect.ValueOf(f).Pointer() == reflect.ValueOf(noopBatchDurable).Pointer()'). Firing logic is split across applyInternal, Batch.SyncWait and commit.go. Otherwise the tracker is cleanly separated.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Concurrency-safe: a mutex guards the waiter min-heap, buffered channels avoid blocking, cancelled waiters are removed from the heap, and close/sync errors are latched. Retention and subscription limits are named constants, and the errors are exported sentinels wrapped with cockroachdb/errors. Minor nit: durations are floored to 1ns (max(..., time.Duration(1))).

items.name: Commit path and public types remain backward compatible
items.name_zh: 提交路径与公共类型保持向后兼容
items.evidence: All new API is additive. Non-sync commits only call noteCommit(), which returns on an atomic load fast path. Timestamps are taken only 'if syncWAL'. NoSyncWait still returns right away and the event fires later in SyncWait. Existing callbacks are untouched; EnsureDefaults only adds the new hook. Sync commits take one tracker mutex, which counts as bookkeeping.
